hints: Set up $V = \pi \int_0^3 y^2 dx = \pi \int_0^3 (x^3 + x^2) dx$.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for the volume obtained by rotating the region under $y = \sqrt{x^3 + x^2}$ around the $x$-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 3$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^3 y^2\,dx = \pi \int_0^3 (x^3 + x^2)\,dx$$

Integrate with respect to $x$ using the power rule:
$$V = \pi \left[ \frac{x^4}{4} + \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_0^3$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = 3$ and lower limit $x = 0$:
$$V = \pi \left( \frac{3^4}{4} + \frac{3^3}{3} - 0 \right) = \pi \left( \frac{81}{4} + 9 \right) = \pi \left( \frac{81 + 36}{4} \right) = \frac{117\pi}{4} \quad (\approx 91.9)$$

hints: Form normal equation $y - 6 = -\frac{4}{11}(x - 3)$ and find the $y$-intercept ($x = 0$).
walkthrough:
Find the $y$-coordinate of point $P$ at $x = 3$:
$$y = \sqrt{3^3 + 3^2} = \sqrt{27 + 9} = \sqrt{36} = 6 \implies P = (3, 6)$$

Differentiate $y = (x^3 + x^2)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}(x^3 + x^2)^{-1/2}(3x^2 + 2x) = \frac{3x^2 + 2x}{2\sqrt{x^3 + x^2}}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal line perpendicular to the curve:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{11/4} = -\frac{4}{11}$$

Write the equation of the normal line passing through $P(3, 6)$ and evaluate the $y$-intercept at $x = 0$:
$$y - 6 = -\frac{4}{11}(x - 3)$$
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y = 6 - \frac{4}{11}(0 - 3) = 6 + \frac{12}{11} = \frac{78}{11} = 7\frac{1}{11} \quad (\approx 7.09)$$
